# Tool Telemetry Complaints

## Goal

Turn an automated Jarela tool telemetry complaint into focused, reviewable fixes without bundling unrelated failures.

Use this for GitHub issues generated by `report_tool_telemetry_issue` or `maybeAutoFileToolTelemetryIssue`, especially issues that list affected tools, success rates, error samples, `min_calls`, and `include_successful` query settings.

## SOP

1. Read the issue before coding.
   - Capture the query settings, affected tools, call counts, sample errors, and any existing maintainer analysis.
   - If the issue covers multiple tools, group them by failure family: validation defect, renamed/deprecated surface, credential/auth problem, transient upstream/network issue, or low-signal one-off.
   - Pick the highest-signal item first: repeated failures, same error class, same argument shape, and a direct owner in this repo.

2. Keep the fix scoped.
   - Start from the named tool implementation or package descriptor.
   - Prefer the package that owns the tool name. For example, `icloud_calendar_*` lives under `packages/icloud-langchain`, while bare `calendar_*` is the native Google Calendar tool.
   - State a falsifiable local hypothesis and one cheap check before editing.
   - Do not refactor unrelated tools while chasing a telemetry report.

3. Fix the root cause.
   - Validation defects: normalize or validate inputs at the owning tool boundary, and make downstream requests use the canonical format expected by the provider.
   - Renamed or removed tools: verify registration first, then either remove stale allowlist entries or add a clear redirect/deprecation stub.
   - Credential failures: improve credential guidance only if the error is reproducible and unclear; do not treat one-off auth failures as implementation bugs without evidence.
   - Low-signal one-off failures: adjust the report/query methodology if the complaint is dominated by `min_calls: 1` noise.

4. Add a regression check.
   - Add or update the narrowest package test that invokes the affected tool or payload builder.
   - Assert on the provider-facing payload or the user-visible error, not just on implementation details.
   - Run the focused test first, then the package typecheck or touched-slice validation.

5. Commit and push.
   - Use a topic branch based on `origin/main` for the PR. If current work sits on a dirty or unrelated branch, cherry-pick the focused fix to a clean branch.
   - Use a Conventional Commit title that can also be the PR title, for example `fix(icloud): use calendar date-time for last-modified`.
   - Let pre-commit hooks run; do not bypass them.
   - Push to the upstream `origin` remote unless explicitly told otherwise.

6. Open the PR.
   - PR title must match Conventional Commits and be suitable for squash merge.
   - Body should include Summary, Validation, and the issue reference.
   - Use `Refs #<issue>` for partial fixes or multi-item telemetry complaints that remain open.
   - Use `Closes #<issue>` only when the PR resolves the issue according to the requested scope, or when the maintainer explicitly wants the issue closed once this fix merges.

7. Reply on the issue.
   - Confirm the reproduced or locally proven failure mode.
   - Link the PR.
   - Explain when it is fixed: "as soon as PR #N merges to `main`; ships in the next patch release after that merge" unless a release branch/tag has already shipped.
   - If using `Closes`, mention that GitHub will close the issue automatically on merge.
   - If only part of the complaint is fixed, say what remains.

8. Close only after the fix is applied.
   - If the PR contains `Closes #<issue>`, let GitHub close the issue on merge.
   - If the PR was merged without an auto-close keyword, verify `mergedAt` or the merge commit first, then close the issue with a comment linking the merged PR.
   - Never close an issue while its fix PR is still open unless the user explicitly instructs you to close it early.

## Useful Commands

```powershell
gh issue view <issue> --repo CircuitWall/jarela --comments --json title,state,body,comments

gh pr create --repo CircuitWall/jarela --base main --head <branch> --title "fix(scope): use imperative subject" --body "..."

gh pr view <pr> --repo CircuitWall/jarela --json state,mergedAt,mergeCommit,url,title

gh issue comment <issue> --repo CircuitWall/jarela --body "..."
```

For multiline GitHub bodies in Windows PowerShell 5.1, prefer a single-quoted here-string assigned to `$body`, then pass `--body "$body"` or `-f body="$body"` to avoid broken Markdown escaping.
